question: The expression \(x^2-y^2-z^2+2yz+x+y-z\) has:
solution:
The terms involving only \(y\) and \(z\) combine into \(-(y-z)^2\). This reveals a difference of squares, whose factor \(x+y-z\) also appears among the remaining terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&x^2-y^2-z^2+2yz+x+y-z\\
&=x^2-(y-z)^2+(x+y-z)\\
&=(x+y-z)(x-y+z)+(x+y-z)\\
&=(x+y-z)(x-y+z+1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Both factors are linear with integer coefficients. In particular, the expression has the factor \(x-y+z+1\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
